title: string.format()
summary: Builds formatted strings from templates: %d integers, %s strings, %f/%.2f floats. Great for timers, prices, and any number-heavy UI text.

details.heading: Common specifiers
details.body: `%d` integer · `%s` string · `%f` float · `%.2f` two decimals · `%q` quoted/escaped string · `%x` hex · `%%` literal percent. Width/padding: `%5d` right-align, `%02d` zero-pad.

details.heading: Alternatives
details.body: Luau interpolated strings `` `Value: {x}` `` cover most cases; string.format wins for numeric formatting (padding, decimals).

explanation.whatItIs: A template filler: describe the shape of your text once, drop values into the slots.
explanation.whyItExists: Concatenating `"0" .. minutes` by hand for zero-padding gets old instantly.
whenNotToUse: Simple text assembly — interpolated strings are cleaner
In extremely hot loops with trivial content
tips: `%02d` = two digits, zero-padded — the timer workhorse
commonMistakes: Wrong specifier type: `%d` with a string argument errors
Forgetting to escape `%` in literal text

examples.title: Timers and prices
examples.code:
local seconds = 125
print(string.format("%02d:%02d", seconds // 60, seconds % 60))  --> 02:05

local price = 19.5
print(string.format("Price: $%.2f", price))   --> Price: $19.50

local ratio = 0.337
print(string.format("%.1f%% complete", ratio * 100))  --> 33.7% complete
